answer: Admission needs signatures that span separate branches of the trust graph. When funding traces tie a newcomer to an operator that already runs k-1 agents, the beacon draws k branches at random, and one vertex in each must sign the newcomer's key. A signature counts only if the graph shows a delta above four hops between its vertex and every vertex that signed for a sibling. A lone agent needs one signature, but an operator's 100 agents need 5,050 from mutually distant strangers, about $252,500 in bribes at $50 each.
